_about: Hand-corrected guide bodies for the Wolff course, transcribed from the page scans (v1 seq 52-53 etc.) because the OCR mangles tables and typewriter faces. Keyed by grammar-topic title as parse-wolff.py emits it; gen-wolff-course.mjs prefers these over OCR prose. Faithful to the book; only OCR errors corrected and layout restored.
Consonants:
Here is a table of the Waray consonant symbols:

| Waray consonants |
|---|
| p t k q h |
| b d g |
| m n ng |
| s |
| w y |
| r |
| l |

In general, these symbols represent sounds which are like their English counterparts, with the following exceptions:

**p, t, k** — pronounced with no explosion of breath following them. Practice them by holding the back of your hand to your mouth and saying *ta* in such a way that no air hits your hand. Do the same for *pa*, *ka*.

**t, d, n** — for Waray *t* (as contrasted with English *t*) the blade of the tongue (the upper side of the tongue just in back of the tip) touches the gums just in back of the upper teeth, and there is no explosion of breath: *Tátay* 'Dad'. Similarly for Waray *d* and *n* — *dara* 'bring', *nábisíta* 'visit', *kadi* 'come'.

**q (glottal stop)** — made by momentarily stopping the air passage at the glottis or Adam's apple, as between the *oh*'s in the English expression of mild alarm *oh-oh!* [oq-o], used for example when you have dropped something, and in the informal negative *hm-mm*. (A glottal stop occurs also in New York pronunciations of *bottle* [boq-l], *little* [liq-l], etc.) The glottal stop at the beginning of a word and between vowels is very weakly pronounced. It is not written in our transcription: an initial vowel, or two successive vowels, indicates a weak glottal stop — e.g. *úukuy* 'dwell' = [qúqukuy].

**ng** — represents the last sound of English *sing*, *going*. The pronunciation exercises will give you practice in making this sound at the beginning of a word, a position it does not occupy in English.

**l** — like *l* in *clean* (i.e. with the tip of the tongue pressed against the roof of the mouth just in back of the upper teeth).
